title: Create a new namespace with a ResourceQuota
prompt: Create namespace 'taskns1'. In it, create a ResourceQuota named 'compute-quota' limiting to max 4 pods, requests.cpu=1, requests.memory=1Gi.
verify: kubectl get ns taskns1 >/dev/null 2>&1 && kubectl get resourcequota compute-quota -n taskns1 -o jsonpath='{.spec.hard.pods}' | grep -q '^4$'

title: etcd snapshot backup
prompt: Take an etcd snapshot from cka-practice-control-plane and save it to /tmp/etcd-backup.db on that node, using the cluster's etcd certs.
verify: docker exec cka-practice-control-plane test -f /tmp/etcd-backup.db

title: Static pod on a node
prompt: Create a static pod named 'static-web' running nginx on cka-practice-worker via the kubelet manifest path (not kubectl apply). Confirm it shows up as '<name>-cka-practice-worker' in 'kubectl get pods'.
verify: kubectl get pod static-web-cka-practice-worker -n default >/dev/null 2>&1

title: Rolling update + rollback
prompt: Create namespace 'taskns4'. Deploy nginx:1.25 as Deployment 'rollme' (2 replicas). Update its image to a bad tag to trigger a failed rollout, then roll back to the previous working revision.
verify: kubectl get deployment rollme -n taskns4 -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}' | grep -q 'nginx:1.25' && kubectl get deployment rollme -n taskns4 -o jsonpath='{.status.readyReplicas}' | grep -q '^2$'

title: Multi-container pod with shared volume
prompt: Create namespace 'taskns5'. Create a Pod 'sidecar-pod' with two containers sharing an emptyDir volume mounted at /data in both: one container (busybox) writes 'hello' to /data/out.txt every 5s, the other (busybox) tails that file.
verify: kubectl get pod sidecar-pod -n taskns5 -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[*].name}' | wc -w | grep -q '^2$'

title: CronJob
prompt: Create namespace 'taskns6'. Create a CronJob 'hello-cron' running every minute that echoes 'hello cka'.
verify: kubectl get cronjob hello-cron -n taskns6 >/dev/null 2>&1

title: ClusterIP + NodePort exposure
prompt: Create namespace 'taskns7'. Deploy nginx (2 replicas, Deployment 'websvc'). Expose it as a ClusterIP Service 'websvc-cip' on port 80, and separately as a NodePort Service 'websvc-np' on port 30080.
verify: kubectl get svc websvc-cip -n taskns7 -o jsonpath='{.spec.type}' | grep -q ClusterIP && kubectl get svc websvc-np -n taskns7 -o jsonpath='{.spec.ports[0].nodePort}' | grep -q 30080

title: NetworkPolicy allow-only-from-namespace
prompt: Create namespaces 'taskns8-a' and 'taskns8-b', each with an nginx pod labeled app=web. In taskns8-a, write a NetworkPolicy 'allow-from-b' that only allows ingress to app=web pods from pods in taskns8-b (any label), denying all else.
verify: kubectl get networkpolicy allow-from-b -n taskns8-a >/dev/null 2>&1

title: Ingress resource
prompt: Create namespace 'taskns9'. Deploy nginx as Deployment 'webapp' + ClusterIP Service 'webapp-svc' port 80. Create an Ingress 'webapp-ing' routing host 'cka.practice.local' path '/' to that service. (An ingress controller isn't required to be installed - just write a correct spec.)
verify: kubectl get ingress webapp-ing -n taskns9 >/dev/null 2>&1

title: PV + PVC + Pod (hostPath, manual binding)
prompt: Create namespace 'taskns10'. Create a PersistentVolume 'manual-pv' (1Gi, hostPath /mnt/data, storageClassName 'manual'), a PVC 'manual-pvc' requesting 1Gi with the same storageClassName, and a Pod mounting it at /usr/share/nginx/html. Confirm the PVC binds to the PV.
verify: kubectl get pvc manual-pvc -n taskns10 -o jsonpath='{.status.phase}' | grep -q Bound

title: Dynamic provisioning with default StorageClass
prompt: Create namespace 'taskns11'. Create a PVC 'dyn-pvc' requesting 500Mi with no storageClassName specified (use cluster default 'standard'). Mount it in a Pod and confirm it auto-provisions and binds.
verify: kubectl get pvc dyn-pvc -n taskns11 -o jsonpath='{.status.phase}' | grep -q Bound

title: Node affinity + tolerations
prompt: Label cka-practice-worker with 'disktype=ssd'. Create namespace 'taskns12'. Create a Deployment 'affine' (nginx, 1 replica) with a nodeAffinity requiring disktype=ssd, and confirm it lands on cka-practice-worker.
verify: kubectl get pod -n taskns12 -l app=affine -o jsonpath='{.items[0].spec.nodeName}' | grep -q cka-practice-worker

title: DaemonSet
prompt: Create namespace 'taskns13'. Create a DaemonSet 'nodelogger' running busybox (command: sleep 3600) that runs one pod on every node, including control-plane (add the needed toleration).
verify: kubectl get daemonset nodelogger -n taskns13 -o jsonpath='{.status.desiredNumberScheduled}' | grep -q '^3$'

title: initContainer gate
prompt: Create namespace 'taskns14'. Create a Pod 'gated-pod' (nginx) with an initContainer (busybox) that runs 'sleep 5' before the main container starts. Confirm the pod reaches Running with both containers accounted for.
verify: kubectl get pod gated-pod -n taskns14 -o jsonpath='{.status.initContainerStatuses[0].state.terminated.reason}' | grep -q Completed

title: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
prompt: Create namespace 'taskns15'. Deploy nginx as Deployment 'hpaapp' (1 replica) with cpu requests set (100m). Create an HPA 'hpaapp-hpa' targeting it, min 1 max 5 replicas, target CPU 50%. (metrics-server isn't installed here, so it won't actually scale - just create a correct spec.)
verify: kubectl get hpa hpaapp-hpa -n taskns15 -o jsonpath='{.spec.maxReplicas}' | grep -q '^5$'

title: Secret from literals, mounted as volume
prompt: Create namespace 'taskns16'. Create a Secret 'app-creds' with keys username=admin, password=s3cr3t via kubectl (not a raw manifest with stringData). Mount it as a volume at /etc/creds (read-only) in a Pod 'creds-pod' (nginx).
verify: kubectl get secret app-creds -n taskns16 >/dev/null 2>&1 && kubectl get pod creds-pod -n taskns16 -o jsonpath='{.spec.volumes[?(@.secret.secretName=="app-creds")].name}' | grep -q .

title: ClusterRole + ClusterRoleBinding
prompt: Create ServiceAccount 'cluster-watcher' in namespace 'default'. Create a ClusterRole 'node-reader' allowing get/list/watch on nodes (cluster-scoped resource). Bind it to the ServiceAccount cluster-wide with a ClusterRoleBinding 'watcher-binding'.
verify: kubectl auth can-i list nodes --as=system:serviceaccount:default:cluster-watcher | grep -q '^yes$'

title: Cordon, drain, uncordon
prompt: Cordon cka-practice-worker2 so no new pods schedule there. Confirm it shows SchedulingDisabled. Then uncordon it again and confirm it's schedulable.
verify: kubectl get node cka-practice-worker2 -o jsonpath='{.spec.unschedulable}' | grep -qv true

title: PriorityClass
prompt: Create a PriorityClass 'high-priority' with value 1000000, not marked as global default. Create namespace 'taskns19'. Create a Pod 'priority-pod' (nginx) using that PriorityClass.
verify: kubectl get pod priority-pod -n taskns19 -o jsonpath='{.spec.priorityClassName}' | grep -q high-priority

title: ExternalName Service
prompt: Create namespace 'taskns20'. Create a Service 'ext-svc' of type ExternalName pointing to 'example.com'.
verify: kubectl get svc ext-svc -n taskns20 -o jsonpath='{.spec.externalName}' | grep -q example.com

title: etcd restore from snapshot
prompt: Namespace 'before-snapshot' already exists. Take an etcd snapshot to /tmp/etcd-restore-test.db on cka-practice-control-plane. Then create namespace 'restore-marker'. Restore etcd from the snapshot into a new data dir (/var/lib/etcd-restored), point etcd's static pod manifest at it, and confirm: 'before-snapshot' still exists (it was there at snapshot time) but 'restore-marker' is gone (it was created after the snapshot).
verify: kubectl get namespace before-snapshot >/dev/null 2>&1 && ! kubectl get namespace restore-marker >/dev/null 2>&1 && docker exec cka-practice-control-plane grep -q etcd-restored /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml

title: Certificate expiration check
prompt: Using kubeadm on cka-practice-control-plane, check the expiration dates of all cluster certificates and save the output to /tmp/cert-expiry.txt on that node.
verify: docker exec cka-practice-control-plane test -f /tmp/cert-expiry.txt && docker exec cka-practice-control-plane grep -q CERTIFICATE /tmp/cert-expiry.txt

title: Expose an existing Deployment (named port)
prompt: A Deployment 'web-server' already exists in namespace 'taskns23' (2 replicas, named container port 'http' = 80). Without editing the Deployment, create a NodePort Service 'web-server-svc' that references the named port 'http' and exposes it on nodePort 30081.
verify: kubectl get svc web-server-svc -n taskns23 -o jsonpath='{.spec.ports[0].nodePort}' | grep -q 30081 && kubectl get endpoints web-server-svc -n taskns23 -o jsonpath='{.subsets[0].addresses[*].ip}' | grep -q .

title: Add a sidecar to an existing Deployment
prompt: A Deployment 'log-app' already exists in namespace 'taskns24', writing lines to /var/log/app/app.log inside an emptyDir volume named 'logs'. Edit the Deployment to add a sidecar container 'log-sidecar' (busybox) that mounts the same 'logs' volume and tails app.log to stdout ('tail -f /var/log/app/app.log').
verify: kubectl get deployment log-app -n taskns24 -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[*].name}' | grep -q log-sidecar && kubectl get pods -n taskns24 -l app=log-app -o jsonpath='{.items[0].status.containerStatuses[?(@.name=="log-sidecar")].ready}' | grep -q true

title: Connect an existing Deployment to an existing ConfigMap
prompt: Namespace 'taskns25' already has a Deployment 'bareapp' and a ConfigMap 'app-config' (key 'greeting'). Edit the Deployment to inject that ConfigMap's 'greeting' key as env var GREETING in the container, without recreating the ConfigMap.
verify: kubectl get deployment bareapp -n taskns25 -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].env[?(@.name=="GREETING")].valueFrom.configMapKeyRef.name}' | grep -q app-config

title: Wire two existing Deployments together via a Service + NetworkPolicy
prompt: Namespace 'taskns26' already has Deployments 'frontend' (nginx) and 'backend' (listens on 8080). Create a ClusterIP Service 'backend-svc' exposing backend port 80 -> targetPort 8080. Then write a NetworkPolicy 'allow-frontend-to-backend' on the backend pods that allows ingress only from pods labeled app=frontend, on port 8080.
verify: kubectl get svc backend-svc -n taskns26 -o jsonpath='{.spec.ports[0].targetPort}' | grep -q 8080 && kubectl get networkpolicy allow-frontend-to-backend -n taskns26 >/dev/null 2>&1

title: Create a StorageClass
prompt: Create a StorageClass named 'slow-tier' using provisioner 'rancher.io/local-path', reclaimPolicy Delete, volumeBindingMode WaitForFirstConsumer.
verify: kubectl get storageclass slow-tier -o jsonpath='{.volumeBindingMode}' | grep -q WaitForFirstConsumer

title: Expand a PVC
prompt: Create namespace 'taskns28'. The default 'standard' StorageClass has allowVolumeExpansion=false, so first create a StorageClass 'growable' (provisioner rancher.io/local-path, volumeBindingMode Immediate, allowVolumeExpansion=true). Then create PVC 'grow-pvc' on that class requesting 100Mi, and expand it to 300Mi.
verify: kubectl get storageclass growable -o jsonpath='{.allowVolumeExpansion}' | grep -q true && kubectl get pvc grow-pvc -n taskns28 -o jsonpath='{.spec.resources.requests.storage}' | grep -q '^300Mi$'

title: PV with Retain reclaim policy
prompt: Create a PersistentVolume 'retain-pv': 1Gi, ReadWriteOnce, hostPath /mnt/retain, storageClassName 'retain-sc', persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy Retain.
verify: kubectl get pv retain-pv -o jsonpath='{.spec.persistentVolumeReclaimPolicy}' | grep -q Retain

title: ConfigMap as a mounted volume
prompt:
Create namespace 'taskns30'. Create ConfigMap 'web-content' with key index.html containing '

hello

'. Run a Pod 'web-content-pod' (nginx) mounting that ConfigMap at /usr/share/nginx/html so curl of the pod returns that HTML.
verify: kubectl exec -n taskns30 web-content-pod -- cat /usr/share/nginx/html/index.html 2>/dev/null | grep -q hello

title: Two pods sharing one PVC
prompt: Create namespace 'taskns31'. Create PVC 'shared-data' (200Mi, storageClassName 'standard'). Run two pods 'writer' and 'reader' on the SAME node, both mounting it at /shared. 'writer' must write /shared/msg.txt containing 'from-writer'; 'reader' must be able to read it.
verify: kubectl exec -n taskns31 reader -- cat /shared/msg.txt 2>/dev/null | grep -q from-writer

title: Expose a Deployment with kubectl expose
prompt: Create namespace 'taskns32' with Deployment 'quickweb' (nginx, 2 replicas). Expose it as a ClusterIP Service named 'quickweb' on port 80 using a single kubectl expose command.
verify: kubectl get svc quickweb -n taskns32 -o jsonpath='{.spec.ports[0].port}' | grep -q '^80$'

title: Multi-port Service
prompt: Create namespace 'taskns33'. Deploy nginx as 'multiport' exposing containerPorts 80 and 8080. Create Service 'multiport-svc' with two NAMED ports: 'web' -> 80 and 'admin' -> 8080.
verify: kubectl get svc multiport-svc -n taskns33 -o jsonpath='{.spec.ports[*].name}' | grep -q web && kubectl get svc multiport-svc -n taskns33 -o jsonpath='{.spec.ports[*].name}' | grep -q admin

title: NetworkPolicy allow by port only
prompt: Create namespace 'taskns34' with an nginx Deployment 'guarded' labeled app=guarded. Write NetworkPolicy 'port-only' that allows ingress to app=guarded pods on TCP 80 from ANY pod in the same namespace, and denies everything else.
verify: kubectl get networkpolicy port-only -n taskns34 -o jsonpath='{.spec.ingress[0].ports[0].port}' | grep -q '^80$'

title: Ingress with two path rules
prompt: Create namespace 'taskns35' with Deployments 'appa' and 'appb' (nginx) plus ClusterIP Services 'appa-svc'/'appb-svc' on port 80. Create Ingress 'split-ing' for host 'split.practice.local' routing /a to appa-svc and /b to appb-svc (pathType Prefix).
verify: [ "$(kubectl get ingress split-ing -n taskns35 -o jsonpath='{.spec.rules[0].http.paths[*].path}' 2>/dev/null | wc -w)" = "2" ]

title: Verify DNS resolution between namespaces
prompt: Create namespaces 'taskns36-a' and 'taskns36-b'. In -a, run nginx Deployment 'crossapp' plus ClusterIP Service 'crossapp-svc' (port 80). In -b, run a long-lived busybox pod named 'crossclient' that can resolve and reach crossapp-svc.taskns36-a.svc.cluster.local.
verify: kubectl exec -n taskns36-b crossclient -- wget -qO- --timeout=5 crossapp-svc.taskns36-a.svc.cluster.local >/dev/null 2>&1

title: Label and annotate a node
prompt: Add label 'workload=batch' and annotation 'owner=practice' to node cka-practice-worker2.
verify: kubectl get node cka-practice-worker2 -o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels.workload}' | grep -q batch && kubectl get node cka-practice-worker2 -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.owner}' | grep -q practice

title: ServiceAccount with a bound Role
prompt: Create namespace 'taskns38'. Create ServiceAccount 'deploy-bot'. Create a Role 'deploy-manager' allowing get/list/create/update on deployments (apps API group), bound to that SA via RoleBinding 'deploy-bot-binding'.
verify: kubectl auth can-i create deployments --as=system:serviceaccount:taskns38:deploy-bot -n taskns38 2>/dev/null | grep -q '^yes$'

title: Read cluster events for triage
prompt: Create namespace 'taskns39'. Deliberately run a pod 'badimage-pod' with image 'nginx:doesnotexist'. Then write the namespace's events, sorted by timestamp, to /tmp/taskns39-events.txt on THIS machine.
verify: test -f /tmp/taskns39-events.txt && grep -qiE 'fail|err|back-off|pull' /tmp/taskns39-events.txt

title: Find top resource-consuming pods without metrics-server
prompt: Without metrics-server, list every pod in the cluster together with its CPU and memory REQUESTS, sorted, and save to /tmp/pod-requests.txt on THIS machine. Hint: kubectl get pods -A -o custom-columns or jsonpath.
verify: test -f /tmp/pod-requests.txt && [ "$(wc -l < /tmp/pod-requests.txt)" -ge 5 ]

title: Drain a node safely and bring it back
prompt: Create namespace 'taskns41' with Deployment 'movable' (nginx, 2 replicas). Drain cka-practice-worker2 (ignore daemonsets, delete emptydir data) so its pods reschedule elsewhere, then uncordon it. End state: node schedulable again AND all 2 replicas Ready.
verify: [ "$(kubectl get node cka-practice-worker2 -o jsonpath='{.spec.unschedulable}' 2>/dev/null)" != "true" ] && [ "$(kubectl get deployment movable -n taskns41 -o jsonpath='{.status.readyReplicas}' 2>/dev/null)" = "2" ]

title: Inspect kubeadm cluster config
prompt: From cka-practice-control-plane, dump the kubeadm ClusterConfiguration held in the kube-system 'kubeadm-config' ConfigMap to /tmp/kubeadm-config.yaml on that node.
verify: docker exec cka-practice-control-plane test -f /tmp/kubeadm-config.yaml && docker exec cka-practice-control-plane grep -q 'kubernetesVersion\|ClusterConfiguration' /tmp/kubeadm-config.yaml

title: Scale a Deployment
prompt: Create namespace 'taskns43' with Deployment 'scaleme' (nginx, 1 replica). Scale it to 4 replicas and confirm all 4 are Ready.
verify: [ "$(kubectl get deployment scaleme -n taskns43 -o jsonpath='{.status.readyReplicas}' 2>/dev/null)" = "4" ]

title: Job with parallelism and completions
prompt: Create namespace 'taskns44'. Create a Job 'parallel-job' (busybox, command: echo done) with completions=6 and parallelism=2. Wait for it to finish successfully.
verify: [ "$(kubectl get job parallel-job -n taskns44 -o jsonpath='{.status.succeeded}' 2>/dev/null)" = "6" ]

title: Pod with resource requests and limits
prompt: Create namespace 'taskns45'. Run Pod 'bounded-pod' (nginx) with requests cpu=100m/memory=128Mi and limits cpu=200m/memory=256Mi. It must reach Running.
verify: kubectl get pod bounded-pod -n taskns45 -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].resources.limits.memory}' | grep -q '^256Mi$' && [ "$(kubectl get pod bounded-pod -n taskns45 -o jsonpath='{.status.phase}')" = "Running" ]

title: Pod anti-affinity across nodes
prompt: Create namespace 'taskns46'. Create Deployment 'spread' (nginx, 2 replicas, label app=spread) with requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution podAntiAffinity on hostname, so the two replicas must land on DIFFERENT nodes. Both must be Ready.
verify: [ "$(kubectl get pods -n taskns46 -l app=spread -o jsonpath='{.items[*].spec.nodeName}' 2>/dev/null | tr ' ' '\n' | sort -u | wc -l)" = "2" ] && [ "$(kubectl get deployment spread -n taskns46 -o jsonpath='{.status.readyReplicas}')" = "2" ]

title: Native sidecar (restartPolicy Always initContainer)
prompt: Create namespace 'taskns47'. Create Deployment 'native-sidecar' (nginx main container) with a NATIVE sidecar: an initContainer named 'logger' (busybox, command 'sleep 3600') that has restartPolicy: Always - the Kubernetes 1.29+ sidecar pattern, GA in 1.35. Deployment must become Ready.
verify: kubectl get deployment native-sidecar -n taskns47 -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.initContainers[?(@.name=="logger")].restartPolicy}' | grep -q Always && [ "$(kubectl get deployment native-sidecar -n taskns47 -o jsonpath='{.status.readyReplicas}')" = "1" ]

title: GatewayClass and Gateway
prompt: Gateway API v1 CRDs are installed. Create namespace 'taskns48'. Create a GatewayClass named 'practice-gc' with controllerName 'example.net/gateway-controller'. Then in taskns48 create a Gateway 'web-gw' using that GatewayClass with a single HTTP listener named 'http' on port 80, allowing routes from the Same namespace.
verify: kubectl get gatewayclass practice-gc -o jsonpath='{.spec.controllerName}' | grep -q 'example.net/gateway-controller' && kubectl get gateway web-gw -n taskns48 -o jsonpath='{.spec.listeners[0].port}' | grep -q '^80$'

title: HTTPRoute attached to a Gateway
prompt: Namespace 'taskns49' already has Deployment 'shop' and Service 'shop-svc' (port 80), plus GatewayClass 'shop-gc' and Gateway 'shop-gw' (HTTP listener on 80). Create an HTTPRoute 'shop-route' that attaches to shop-gw via parentRefs, matches hostname 'shop.practice.local', and forwards path prefix '/' to shop-svc on port 80.
verify: kubectl get httproute shop-route -n taskns49 -o jsonpath='{.spec.parentRefs[0].name}' | grep -q shop-gw && kubectl get httproute shop-route -n taskns49 -o jsonpath='{.spec.rules[0].backendRefs[0].name}' | grep -q shop-svc

title: HTTPRoute traffic splitting by weight
prompt: Namespace 'taskns50' already has Services 'v1-svc' and 'v2-svc' (both port 80), a GatewayClass and Gateway 'split-gw'. Create an HTTPRoute 'canary-route' attached to split-gw that sends 90% of traffic to v1-svc and 10% to v2-svc using backendRef weights.
verify: w=$(kubectl get httproute canary-route -n taskns50 -o jsonpath='{.spec.rules[0].backendRefs[*].weight}' 2>/dev/null); echo "$w" | grep -q 90 && echo "$w" | grep -q 10

title: Cross-namespace HTTPRoute with ReferenceGrant
prompt: Namespace 'taskns51-gw' has Gateway 'shared-gw' (listener allows routes from All namespaces). Namespace 'taskns51-app' has Service 'remote-svc' (port 80). In taskns51-app create an HTTPRoute 'remote-route' whose parentRef points at shared-gw in taskns51-gw (cross-namespace), and create the ReferenceGrant in taskns51-gw that permits it.
verify: kubectl get httproute remote-route -n taskns51-app -o jsonpath='{.spec.parentRefs[0].namespace}' | grep -q taskns51-gw && kubectl get referencegrant -n taskns51-gw -o name 2>/dev/null | grep -q referencegrant

title: Create a join token for a new worker
prompt: On cka-practice-control-plane, create a NEW bootstrap token and produce the full 'kubeadm join' command a fresh worker would run. Save that command to /tmp/join-command.txt on that node. (Don't actually join a node - just generate it.)
verify: docker exec cka-practice-control-plane test -f /tmp/join-command.txt && docker exec cka-practice-control-plane grep -q 'kubeadm join' /tmp/join-command.txt && docker exec cka-practice-control-plane grep -q 'discovery-token-ca-cert-hash' /tmp/join-command.txt && [ "$(docker exec cka-practice-control-plane kubeadm token list 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2 | wc -l)" -ge 2 ]

title: Renew the apiserver certificate
prompt: On cka-practice-control-plane, renew ONLY the apiserver certificate with kubeadm, then write the fresh 'kubeadm certs check-expiration' output to /tmp/renewed-certs.txt on that node. The apiserver cert's expiry must be later than the other certs', proving it was reissued.
verify: docker exec cka-practice-control-plane test -f /tmp/renewed-certs.txt && docker exec cka-practice-control-plane sh -c 'test $(openssl x509 -enddate -noout -in /etc/kubernetes/pki/apiserver.crt | cut -d= -f2 | xargs -I{} date -d "{}" +%s) -gt $(openssl x509 -enddate -noout -in /etc/kubernetes/pki/apiserver-kubelet-client.crt | cut -d= -f2 | xargs -I{} date -d "{}" +%s)'

title: Check what an upgrade would do
prompt: On cka-practice-control-plane, run the kubeadm command that reports which versions this cluster can upgrade to, and save its full output to /tmp/upgrade-plan.txt on that node.
verify: docker exec cka-practice-control-plane test -f /tmp/upgrade-plan.txt && docker exec cka-practice-control-plane grep -qi 'cluster version' /tmp/upgrade-plan.txt

title: Upgrade a cluster with kubeadm (needs upgrade-lab)
prompt: Run './upgrade-lab.sh up' first - it builds a separate 'cka-upgrade' cluster at v1.35.0. Upgrade its CONTROL-PLANE node to v1.35.8 the exam way: drain the node, put the v1.35.8 kubeadm binary in place, 'kubeadm upgrade apply v1.35.8', upgrade kubelet, restart it, uncordon. The node must report v1.35.8 and be Ready. ('./upgrade-lab.sh task' reprints these steps, 'down' cleans up.)
verify: kubectl --context kind-cka-upgrade get node cka-upgrade-control-plane -o jsonpath='{.status.nodeInfo.kubeletVersion}' 2>/dev/null | grep -q 'v1.35.8'
